```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The 90-day goal is decisive. Brief B cites the seed company's own founder: roughly 5 months of in-person trust-building per closed deal. That is direct, sourced evidence that B's main channel cannot produce a paying customer inside the window, and the brief gives no reason AI agents would shorten it.",
    "Brief A shows self-serve purchasing at low price points. CrankWheel's Solo plan is $29/mo and Blitzz charges about $15-19/agent/mo, both sourced. A small support team could plausibly put a card down without a sales cycle, and A names two async channels (Google Ads, Zendesk Marketplace) that don't depend on founder office visits.",
    "B's second channel is not available in time. The PestWorld booth costs $3,475-$4,500 and 2026 booths are already sold out.",
    "B has the stronger proof that the category makes money (dashp at about $100k ARR, D2DHQ's published $149-$499/mo pricing). But that proof comes with a small ICP the founder describes as 'hundreds' of companies, at least 6 direct competitors, and another solo builder running the same playbook. Proof the market pays does not overcome a sales cycle longer than the deadline.",
    "A has serious weaknesses that keep this close. Free substitutes exist (Quick Assist, JoinByKey). Compliance gates (SOC 2, HIPAA) likely block regulated buyers. The '41% faster / 47% higher FCR' figures have no source, so I counted them as missing. A is still the bet where a first small payer within 90 days is plausible on the evidence given."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence doesn't come from the payer. One quote is a pest control tech's complaint on a complaints site. The other is a lawsuit over $217k in unpaid commissions. Both show that reps experience wage disputes. Neither shows that company owners, the stated payers, want or will pay for commission-tracking software. If anything, they suggest some owners benefit from opacity.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-low confidence. Neither brief has sourced evidence from its actual payer. A's demand quotes come from family caregivers, not support managers. B's come from reps, not owners. A wins mainly because B's own evidence documents a sales cycle longer than 90 days, not because A has proven B2B demand. If A's small-team segment turns out to need compliance certifications before a pilot, A's timeline also breaks."
}
```
